incident_description: A production-impacting malfunction was opened for UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) after the system stopped at bag-out after sorting. Case and chat evidence indicate the site manually bagged out while support investigated AGV/robot sequencing or task-related issues. Supporting evidence includes reports that an AGV had not moved for 3 hours, that bag-out started and then stopped again, and that an HMI associated with the hospital area showed a fault. The source also notes this had occurred before according to the customer.
customer_operational_impact: Production was seriously impacted. The site reported the system would not complete bag-out after sorting, required manual bagging out, and needed AGVs moving for the next sort.
what_resolved_it: Support guidance focused on restoring proper AGV/robot sequence. Case resolution notes state that when AGVs/robots were back in proper sequence, the customer confirmed they were functional and the call ended. Additional evidence shows robots were turned off due to low batteries, later turned back on, and remained on, but the exact decisive recovery step is not fully isolated in the source.
follow_up_required: SME review recommended to confirm the exact recovery action and whether the primary issue was AGV sequence, stuck task, exchange pair behavior, or another related condition.
Review whether HMI/task visibility gaps at site contributed to troubleshooting difficulty.
Review recurring issue history because the case intake states the problem had occurred before according to the customer.
support_boundary: FORTNA technical support handled the case and escalated to another department during troubleshooting. Evidence also indicates limited screen visibility in Aveva and reliance on site-side observations and HMI/RMS context.
